titel: Emperor Constantine the Great: Christianity and the Roman Empire

einzeiler: A deep dive into the life, reign, and religious transformation of Constantine the Great.
kurzfassung: Greg Jenner is joined by historian Lucy Grigg and comedian Ivo Graham to explore the turbulent life and legacy of Roman Emperor Constantine the Great. The discussion covers his humble family origins, the complex politics of the Tetrarchy, and his pivotal conversion to Christianity. The episode also examines his bloody path to absolute power, the founding of Constantinople, and the heavy reliance on polarized and forged historical sources.
stichpunkte: Constantine's father was a rising military commander, while his mother Helena had humble origins.
The Tetrarchy was established by Diocletian as a system of rule by four to stabilize the empire.
Constantine fled across Europe on fast horses to escape a hostile court and joined his father in Britain.
Following his father's death in York in 306, Constantine was proclaimed emperor by his troops.
The decisive Battle of the Milvian Bridge in 312 marked Constantine's victory over Maxentius.
Constantine allegedly saw a heavenly sign before the battle, sparking his association with Christianity.
He convened the Council of Nicaea in 325, helping to establish core Christian doctrine like the Nicene Creed.
Constantine executed his eldest son Crispus and his wife Fausta under mysterious and debated circumstances in 326.
He founded a new imperial capital at Byzantium, naming it Constantinople and inaugurating it in 330.
Constantine was baptized on his deathbed in 337 shortly before his planned campaign against the Persians.

clips.hook: Comparing Roman emperor turnover to modern football managers.
clips.text: The hosts draw a parallel between the rapid turnover of Roman emperors during a period of instability and modern football clubs cycling through managers.

clips.hook: A high-stakes escape across the Roman Empire on horseback.
clips.text: Fearing for his life, Constantine executed a desperate escape across the empire by commandeering the fastest horses at relay stations and sabotaging the animals behind him to prevent pursuit.

clips.hook: How historical religious heresies got their names.
clips.text: The discussion explains that in early Christian theological disputes, the winning faction would label the opposing view a heresy and name it after a specific person.

clips.hook: The grim and debated fate of Constantine's wife.
clips.text: Historical accounts suggest that Fausta was executed by being locked in an overheated bathhouse, though anti-Constantinian sources claimed she was involved in an incestuous affair with her stepson.

clips.hook: Uncovering one of history's greatest document forgeries.
clips.text: A Renaissance humanist and priest eventually proved that a foundational medieval document granting massive temporal power to the Pope was entirely fake.

beschreibung:
Greg Jenner is joined in ancient Rome by Professor Lucy Grig and comedian Ivo Graham to learn all about Emperor Constantine the Great and the Christianisation of the Roman empire. Born not in Rome but in the Balkans, Constantine’s life was shaped by the turbulent politics of the late third century. He grew up as Emperor Diocletian – remembered now as a savage persecutor of Christians – was establishing the Tetrarchy, with four rulers now in control of the empire. One of these was Constantine’s father, Constantius. But when Constantius died in York, his son was acclaimed emperor in his place, kicking off a violent civil war. This episode traces Constantine’s life, from his childhood through to his elevation as emperor, taking in his extraordinary victory at Milvian Bridge, the vision that allegedly encouraged his conversion to Christianity, and his founding of Constantinople as a New Rome. It also examines his relationship with his mother, later known as Saint Helena, the bloody path he carved to the imperial throne, and his role in the pivotal Council of Nicaea, a landmark event in Christian history.
If you’re a fan of religious revolutions, bloody Roman power politics, and historical nepo babies, you’ll love our episode on Constantine the Great.

If you want more Roman rulers, listen to our episodes on the Rise of Julius Caesar, Agrippina the Younger, or Emperor Nero, with Professor Mary Beard and Patton Oswalt. And for more on the Christianisation of the Roman empire, check out our episode on Hypatia of Alexandria.
